meta.title: Ch 1: Quality Control / Quality Management — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 1 (Quality Control / Quality Management).

questions.q: A firm's system of quality management is designed to provide reasonable assurance that:
o: The firm and its personnel comply with professional standards and issue appropriate reports
questions.why: The quality-management standard for firms (successor framing to SQC 1) targets compliance with professional standards and reports appropriate in the circumstances — reasonable, not absolute; appropriate, not unqualified.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — reports are 'appropriate in the circumstances', the wording examiners guard AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Quality management is the firm's immune system, engagement by engagement.

questions.q: An engagement quality control/review is intended to:
o: Provide an objective evaluation of significant judgments and conclusions before the report is issued
Review only the working papers' indexing
questions.why: EQR is an objective check on significant judgments and conclusions by a reviewer not part of the team, BEFORE report date; it supplements, never replaces, the engagement partner's responsibility, and its completion timing is a favourite trap.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — before the report — and it never replaces the partner AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A second pair of eyes earns value only by arriving before the signature.

questions.q: A disagreement between the engagement partner and the EQR reviewer on a significant matter:
o: Is resolved in favour of the reviewer
Must be resolved before the report is issued, following the firm's consultation policy
questions.why: Firms' policies require differences of opinion to be documented and resolved; the report cannot be dated while an unresolved difference exists — same discipline as consultation.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — unresolved difference = no report date Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

questions.q: Audit documentation is assembled on a final basis and retained:
o: For the period required by regulation (long enough for legal and inspection needs — firms set and document it)
questions.why: Retention periods are set by regulation and firm policy (currently a multi-year minimum under the SAs' documentation framework); the file is assembled within a short window after the report and is not deleted or overwritten after assembly except for documented reasons.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the two clocks: assembly window vs retention period AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: You can add to the fire; you can't burn it.

questions.q: An engagement quality review must be completed:
o: By the date of the auditor's report
questions.why: The standard ties the review's completion to report issuance — an EQR that arrives late protects nothing.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the date anchor is the whole answer AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The second look must come before the first signature.

questions.q: A firm's consultation policy on difficult matters requires documentation of:
o: The parties, the consultation process, and the conclusions reached and accepted
questions.why: Consultation documentation covers who, how, and what was concluded — and the reviewer/consultant conclusions bind the engagement.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — documentation is the audit trail of advice Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Advice without a memo is folklore.

questions.q: ICAI's move from SQC 1 to the quality-management framework (SQCS) changes the firm's duty from checklist systems to:
o: A risk-based system: quality objectives, identified quality risks, and designed responses, monitored and remediated
questions.why: DEFINITE structural change: the firm must design its system against ITS quality risks (the entity-specific quality objectives → risks → responses chain), plus monitoring/remediation and the EQR triggers — the vocabulary shift from 'policies and procedures' to 'system of quality management' is the amendment's signature.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the shift is from boxes to risks AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Quality management standards replacing SQC 1
mem.tip: Checklists prevent routine slips; risk systems prevent novel ones.

questions.q: Under the quality management standards, an engagement quality review (EQR):
o: Is required for audits of listed entities and other engagements per firm policy defined by criteria
Is performed by the engagement team leader
questions.why: EQR is mandatory for listed-entity audits (and wherever the firm's policy, set on defined criteria, says so); the reviewer must be sufficiently competent, independent of the engagement, and assigned per eligibility rules — and crucially, the review does not reduce the engagement partner's responsibility.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — a second pair of eyes, never a spare signature AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The reviewer adds judgment, not absolution.

questions.q: A firm's quality management system must include a process for:
o: Complaints and allegations about departures from standards, with defined evaluation, investigation and remedial action
questions.why: The complaints channel is a feedback loop feeding the corrective-action pipeline: log, evaluate, investigate, act, and report results to the governing body — silence in the system is itself a QM finding.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — a complaint is a free risk assessment Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The hotline is the smoke detector of the quality system.

questions.q: Declining an audit because of doubts about management integrity is required by quality management under:
o: Client acceptance/continuance policies weighing integrity, competence and ethical issues
questions.why: Acceptance decisions weigh the client's integrity, the firm's competence/capacity to perform, and ethical requirements — any of the three failing is a reason to decline even when the fee is attractive.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — three-question gate before every engagement AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The best client to refuse is the one you cannot trust.

questions.q: An engagement quality reviewer must be:
o: Enough in seniority and competence, not part of the engagement team, and free of objectivity impairment
questions.why: EQR criteria: partner (or equivalent) with competence, authority, integrity, sufficient and appropriate time — AND not a member of the engagement team (the objectivity line).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — reviewer ≠ doer Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

questions.q: Firm-level monitoring of engagement quality typically includes:
o: Periodic inspection of completed engagements (cold file reviews), including by external inspectors where required
questions.why: Monitoring = ongoing + periodic inspection of completed files against standards — the cold-review loop with remediation tracking is what makes a quality system self-healing.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — inspect yesterday to fix tomorrow Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A quality system without a look-back is a promise without a receipt.
